_meta.description: LLM-authored due-diligence judgments per component, keyed by ecosystem/name. Authored by the Mistral LLM assistant in a Vibe session on 2026-11-12 from evidence.json + maintainers.json + curated.json. Consumed by assess_component.py as the analysis layer; overall tiers are computed from these statuses deterministically.

npm/express.assessment: OpenJS-stewarded with a technical committee, published security policy and prompt CVE patching (2024 fixes shipped well before the pinned 5.x line); high trust.

criterion_notes.c02_known_vulnerabilities: Documented CVE history (CVE-2024-43796, CVE-2024-45590) fixed in versions predating the pinned line; only an automated OSV pass remains.

npm/socket.io.assessment: Very active, org-backed project with a strong coordinated-disclosure record; high trust despite no SECURITY.md at the repo root.

criterion_notes.c06_additional_cybersecurity_testing: bidirectional realtime channel: include auth/origin validation in penetration testing.

npm/socket.io-client.assessment: Ships from the same active socket.io monorepo and shares its patch cadence and advisory exposure.

criterion_notes.c06_additional_cybersecurity_testing: same realtime-channel exposure as socket.io.

npm/svelte.assessment: Core-team-maintained compiler under active daily development; the product must compensate at the app layer for the inherent XSS exposure of client templating.

criterion_notes.c06_additional_cybersecurity_testing: client-rendering framework: XSS-focused review of web app output hardening is required.

npm/react.assessment: Meta-stewarded with mature release engineering and disclosure practices; risk concentrates in usage patterns rather than the library itself.

npm/react-dom.assessment: Same Meta-stewarded monorepo as react with identical advisory and release process.

npm/ioredis.assessment: Actively maintained within the Redis Ltd.-supported ecosystem with regular releases; solid maintenance organization.

npm/postgres.assessment: Genuinely maintained by its originator with a stable, well-audited codebase, but a small core team makes organizational continuity the main uncertainty.

npm/dom-to-image.assessment: Unmaintained since April 2024 with no release cadence and no disclosure channel, yet it renders user-influenced DOM in the product: replace it; patch capability cannot be presumed.

criterion_notes.c13_intended_use_alignment: intended use is technically as-designed, but the maintenance posture makes continuing this use inadvisable.
criterion_notes.c05_risk_assessment: highest-risk component in the SBOM: stale upstream plus untrusted-input exposure.

npm/qrcode.assessment: Effectively dormant upstream since mid-2024 with no disclosure process; low complexity limits impact but a future CVE would likely go unpatched.

criterion_notes.c05_risk_assessment: moderate-high: stale upstream; monitor for CVEs and pre-plan a replacement.

npm/uuid.assessment: Small, well-understood, org-maintained and actively pushed; minimal complexity makes residual risk very low.

npm/hls.js.assessment: Active video-dev community project processing streamed, potentially untrusted media; strong cadence and good advisory history.

criterion_notes.c06_additional_cybersecurity_testing: consumes untrusted media manifests: include in ingest-path fuzzing.

npm/sanitize-filename.assessment: Single-maintainer but pushed this month; tiny, easily reviewable surface; acceptable with periodic source review.

criterion_notes.c11_security_by_design_indicators: small project; verify the implementation directly during technical verification rather than relying on upstream SBD claims.

npm/@nestjs/core.assessment: Large framework organization with a published security policy and continuous releases; core framework trust is high.

criterion_notes.c02_known_vulnerabilities: no open issues known to the analyst; wire an OSV scan for confirmation.
criterion_notes.c04_vulnerability_disclosure_process: published SECURITY.md in the nestjs monorepo.

npm/@nestjs/swagger.assessment: Maintained within the nestjs organization but with a slower, uneven cadence than core; verify activity before external conformity claims.

npm/@noble/hashes.assessment: Audited cryptographic library with published audits and disciplined minimal-surface design; security-relevant hashing: pin and keep current.

criterion_notes.c11_security_by_design_indicators: published third-party audits; constant-time discipline; exemplary for its size class.

npm/bcrypt.assessment: Kelektiv-org maintained native port of a decades-audited algorithm; algorithmic maturity compensates for the modest maintenance organization.

criterion_notes.c06_additional_cybersecurity_testing: password hashing: validate cost parameters and native build provenance during technical verification.

npm/bullmq.assessment: Commercially backed by taskforce.sh with very active releases; job payloads are semi-trusted input, so queue handlers deserve testing.

criterion_notes.c06_additional_cybersecurity_testing: job payloads cross a trust boundary: test handler input validation.

npm/chokidar.assessment: Widely-deployed file watcher under an expert individual maintainer; small attack surface, moderate continuity risk.

npm/cookie.assessment: jshttp-org maintained, RFC-conformant parsing central to auth flows; small, scrutinized, spec-driven codebase.

npm/fluent-ffmpeg.assessment: Thin wrapper maintained at low cadence; the ffmpeg binary it drives is the real security boundary - treat wrapper inputs as untrusted and keep the external binary current.

criterion_notes.c06_additional_cybersecurity_testing: wraps a parser of untrusted media: test argument construction and ffmpeg binary provenance.

npm/geo-tz.assessment: Single-maintainer offline timezone lookup; simple, mostly static data; low residual risk but no organizational safety net.

npm/handlebars.assessment: Known ReDoS/prototype-pollution history with patches published when disclosed; template compilation of user-influenced templates would be dangerous - the product uses designer-controlled templates only.

criterion_notes.c13_intended_use_alignment: safe only because templates are app-controlled; document this constraint.
criterion_notes.c06_additional_cybersecurity_testing: if runtime user templates are ever introduced, sandbox compilation immediately.

npm/js-yaml.assessment: Nodeca-org YAML parser with known ReDoS history promptly fixed; parses developer-controlled configs in this product, keeping exposure limited.

criterion_notes.c13_intended_use_alignment: parses app-owned YAML (codegen), not user uploads; keep it that way.

npm/kysely.assessment: Active org-run typed SQL builder with strong typing discipline; SQL construction review is the meaningful extra test.

criterion_notes.c06_additional_cybersecurity_testing: verify no dynamic SQL string interpolation bypasses parameterization in queries.

npm/lodash-es.assessment: Feature-frozen but universally deployed; the 2020 prototype-pollution fix (4.17.19) shows issues do get patched; reliability over innovation is the norm.

criterion_notes.c05_risk_assessment: low residual risk: mature and stable; substitution churn would exceed benefit.

npm/archiver.assessment: Org-maintained archive builder on a sensitive output path; past path-traversal fixes in 7.x show responsive patching.

criterion_notes.c06_additional_cybersecurity_testing: archive generation from user content: test produced archives for zip-slip/path traversal.

npm/maplibre-gl.assessment: Community-coalition (MapLibre org) with corporate users co-maintaining; active; renders map data of untrusted provenance in the browser.

criterion_notes.c06_additional_cybersecurity_testing: renders externally sourced vector tiles: XSS and resource-exhaustion review warranted.

npm/multer.assessment: Express-org maintained upload handler, one of the most security-scrutinized components of its niche, directly on the untrusted upload path.

criterion_notes.c06_additional_cybersecurity_testing: upload boundary: fuzz filename/content-type handling; verify size and count limits in product config.

npm/nodemailer.assessment: Veteran maintainer, highest-deployment email library with consistent patch releases; header handling is the sensitive surface.

npm/openid-client.assessment: Certified OIDC implementation by a dedicated authentication-ecosystem maintainer with conformance tests and rapid security fixes; auth-critical.

criterion_notes.c06_additional_cybersecurity_testing: OAuth/OIDC flows are intrusion-facing: include in penetration testing of the product.

npm/picomatch.assessment: Micromatch-ecosystem glob engine with ReDoS history fixed long ago and expert maintenance; used on path patterns in tooling here.

npm/semver.assessment: npm Inc.-maintained reference implementation; 2022 ReDoS (CVE-2022-25883) patched across all majors within days; exemplary patch discipline.

npm/sharp.assessment: Top-tier individual maintainer with an exceptional security record around image decoding, Vercel-affiliated in practice; heavily exercised by downstream users.

criterion_notes.c11_security_by_design_indicators: memory-safe via libvips abstractions and rapid fixes to libvips CVEs; add per-release regression checks.
criterion_notes.c06_additional_cybersecurity_testing: primary product entry point for untrusted image bytes: mandatory fuzz corpus.

npm/sirv.assessment: Small, expert-maintained static file server by its originator; serving checks (path traversal guards) are its whole security surface.

npm/ua-parser-js.assessment: Survivor of a 2021 supply-chain compromise that responded properly (recut versions, verified publisher); current development is active and patch-responsive; strict version pinning is essential given this history.

criterion_notes.c11_security_by_design_indicators: the 2021 compromise and clean recovery is evidence of a functioning process; keep publisher verification in the pipeline.
criterion_notes.c05_risk_assessment: moderate: prior compromise means integrity controls (lockfile, provenance) must stay strict.

npm/validator.assessment: Community-org maintained with steady releases; input-validation function is SBD-adjacent by nature.

criterion_notes.c06_additional_cybersecurity_testing: validation library: test that the product rejects invalid input rather than relying on normalizing transforms.

npm/zod.assessment: Extremely popular type-validation library with team-backed development and corporate adopters; validation-by-design is inherently SBD.

criterion_notes.c07_technical_verification: runtime schema validation: verify product schemas reject unexpected fields (no passthrough).

npm/async-lock.assessment: Single-maintainer, low-churn, tiny utility; correctness matters more than activity here; periodic review suffices.

npm/nestjs-otel.assessment: Individual-maintained integration shim over the CNCF engine; small surface, narrow API; monitor for abandonment.

npm/svelte-i18n.assessment: Widely-installed i18n helper by its originator; effectively feature-complete; low complexity keeps risk low despite individual stewardship.

npm/@photo-sphere-viewer/core.assessment: Dedicated originator with a long plugin lineage; renders photo content - XSS attention in product usage recommended.

criterion_notes.c06_additional_cybersecurity_testing: renders media in the DOM: review script/URL injection vectors in product usage.

npm/@simplewebauthn/server.assessment: Focused, standards-driven passkey implementation by its originator with conformance tests; auth-critical like openid-client.

criterion_notes.c06_additional_cybersecurity_testing: auth-critical: include passkey ceremonies in penetration testing.

npm/@tanstack/svelte-query.assessment: TanStack team maintained, extremely widely deployed data layer; professional organization with consistent release discipline.

npm/@mdi/js.assessment: Icon data package by the Pictogrammers org; static asset data, no parsing, negligible attack surface.

npm/@opentelemetry/api.assessment: CNCF-stewarded standard API with maximal ecosystem scrutiny and active governance.

npm/@opentelemetry/context-async-hooks.assessment: Same CNCF stewardship; runtime context plumbing, moderate complexity.

npm/@opentelemetry/instrumentation-http.assessment: CNCF HTTP instrumentation wraps request paths: test under production-like traffic.

npm/@opentelemetry/resources.assessment: CNCF resource model types; same governance.

npm/@opentelemetry/sdk-node.assessment: CNCF node SDK bundle; same governance.

npm/@opentelemetry/semantic-conventions.assessment: CNCF convention constants; data-only, negligible surface.

pypi/fastapi.assessment: Team-maintained with corporate sponsorship and an exceptionally large deployment base; pydantic-based input validation by design is strong SBD by construction.

criterion_notes.c06_additional_cybersecurity_testing: API framework: middleware config (CORS/auth) and file endpoints are the product's responsibility.

pypi/uvicorn.assessment: Encode-org maintained, healthy release cadence; core async HTTP server of the ML service.

criterion_notes.c04_vulnerability_disclosure_process: encode has published GHSA advisories on request-smuggling-adjacent issues; process evidence exists.

pypi/pydantic.assessment: Corporately stewarded (Pydantic Services Inc.), industry-defining type-validation library; strict-by-design input validation is security architecture, not just a feature.

criterion_notes.c11_security_by_design_indicators: strict non-coercive validation defaults are de-facto secure-input design.
criterion_notes.c02_known_vulnerabilities: ReDoS-class issues in the 2.x line were patched and disclosed promptly; pin the current minor.

pypi/pydantic-settings.assessment: Same Pydantic Inc. stewardship; configuration parsing only.

pypi/pillow.assessment: Community-org maintained with the best long-term CVE patching record in Python image handling; keep current: imaging is the product's hottest attack surface.

criterion_notes.c06_additional_cybersecurity_testing: mandatory CVE watch and fuzz corpus for every version bump.
criterion_notes.c02_known_vulnerabilities: recurring image-decoder CVEs, consistently patched within days by python-pillow.

pypi/numpy.assessment: NumFOCUS-backed reference project; numerical core rarely changes, but its ubiquity means vulnerabilities surface fast and get fixed by funded maintainers.

pypi/opencv-python-headless.assessment: Corporate-maintained (OpenCV org) wheels over the C++ flagship; wheel-era issues fixed actively; upstream audit history is a proxy for process maturity.

criterion_notes.c02_known_vulnerabilities: wheel-era issues fixed upstream; track OpenCV security bulletins.

pypi/onnx.assessment: Linux-Foundation-held model format standard; corporate multi-party stewardship; model files are data, not code, in the product.

pypi/onnxruntime-gpu.assessment: Microsoft-maintained inference engine with a published support policy and active CVE response; executes untrusted third-party model files inside the product.

criterion_notes.c06_additional_cybersecurity_testing: model inference executes untrusted graph structures: constrain model provenance; sandbox the ML container.

pypi/huggingface-hub.assessment: Hugging Face Inc.-maintained with rapid releases; the 2024 deserialization issues revived the lesson that model downloads are untrusted payloads - treat them as such.

criterion_notes.c02_known_vulnerabilities: CVE-2024-23651/23652/23653 fixed promptly; loading remains trust-tracked by the product.

pypi/tokenizers.assessment: Hugging Face-maintained Rust-backed tokenizer with active releases; parsing untrusted text is its purpose; upstream test coverage is high.

pypi/python-multipart.assessment: Community org resumed stewardship and patched the 2023-2024 ReDoS/DoS issues quickly; upload boundary component - keep current.

criterion_notes.c02_known_vulnerabilities: CVE-2023-31047 and the 2024 ReDoS issues all fixed in released versions.

pypi/gunicorn.assessment: Individual-maintained but functionally frozen, with a sparse but real security-patch history around request smuggling; pin the current major and test headers at the proxy.

criterion_notes.c02_known_vulnerabilities: request-smuggling class CVEs fixed upstream; test the reverse-proxy pairing in deployment.

pypi/rapidocr.assessment: RapidAI community org; wraps onnxruntime with preprocessing; moderate complexity; keep pinned and model-provenance-verified.

pypi/orjson.assessment: Single expert maintainer, Rust memory safety, high-performance JSON parsing of untrusted payloads; rapid patch turnaround observed historically.

criterion_notes.c11_security_by_design_indicators: memory-safe language choice and exhaustive fuzzing in the repo are genuine SBD indicators.

pub/flutter.assessment: Google-maintained framework with a formal release process, security page and coordinated disclosure; industrial quality bar.

criterion_notes.c04_vulnerability_disclosure_process: flutter/flutter publishes a security policy and posts security advisories; process evidence is public.

pub/drift.assessment: Single-origin but professionally run (extensive docs, formal query API, large deployment base); product-critical SQLite layer.

criterion_notes.c06_additional_cybersecurity_testing: verify drift's query API is used exclusively (no raw SQL interpolation) in mobile code review.

pub/flutter_secure_storage.assessment: Community-org plugin over Keychain/Keystore; credential storage is the most sensitive mobile surface.

criterion_notes.c06_additional_cybersecurity_testing: audit storage configuration options (encryptedSharedPreferences, accessibility flags).

pub/flutter_local_notifications.assessment: Community-maintained by a long-tenured maintainer; minor attack surface, but configuration mistakes (deep-link handling) are common.

pub/geolocator.assessment: Baseflow-corporate-maintained plugin; location is privacy-sensitive but the plugin itself is thin; standard governance.

pub/connectivity_plus.assessment: Community-org plus_plugins coalition; capability detection only, small surface.

pub/hooks_riverpod.assessment: Single-origin but fiercely maintained state-management standard with a documented API stability policy.

pub/auto_route.assessment: Individual-maintained routing library; codegen-dependent, moderate complexity; guard for abandonment but integration risk is contained.

pub/http.assessment: Dart/Google-maintained standard HTTP client with team stewardship; request forgery risk is handled by the product, not the package.

criterion_notes.c06_additional_cybersecurity_testing: SSRF review belongs at the product layer: audit user-supplied URLs passed to this client.

cargo/cbindgen.assessment: Mozilla-lineage build-time tool used only in codegen (not shipped in the product binary); maintenance quality matters little to runtime security.

criterion_notes.c13_intended_use_alignment: build-time dependency: excluded from shipped runtime artifacts.

cargo/jni.assessment: jni-rs org maintained Rust FFI bindings; the unsafe boundary is exactly the region the product lints (undocumented_unsafe_blocks=deny).

criterion_notes.c07_technical_verification: FFI boundary: required target of technical code review.

cargo/libc.assessment: Rust-project maintained, effectively frozen spec-mapping crate with rigorous review culture.

cargo/rayon.assessment: Data-parallelism standard by Rust core-adjacent maintainers; mature, conservative changes.

cargo/quick_cache.assessment: Individual-maintained cache library; bounded-space logic is the safety-relevant property; review during technical verification.

cargo/jxl.assessment: libjxl-org (Google-affiliated authors) Rust decoder with trustpub-verified publishing, a heavy conformance corpus and very frequent releases; excellent for its age.

criterion_notes.c06_additional_cybersecurity_testing: parses untrusted JPEG XL bytes on mobile: include in the media fuzz corpus.
criterion_notes.c11_security_by_design_indicators: trustpub/CI-verified publishing plus many releases since 2025 is strong evidence of a disciplined process.

cargo/moxcms.assessment: Exceptional release velocity with very heavy downstream adoption, but single-maintainer bus-factor with no published security policy; the pinch point of the native color pipeline.

criterion_notes.c10_oss_stewardship: individually maintained with commercial-grade activity but not formally stewarded for commercial purposes.
criterion_notes.c05_risk_assessment: moderate: activity high, organization thin; code review and exact version pinning required.
criterion_notes.c06_additional_cybersecurity_testing: processes color profile data from untrusted images: include in the native fuzz corpus.

cargo/pic-scale.assessment: Same single maintainer as moxcms with very active releases; SIMD-heavy scaling code on untrusted image geometry data.

criterion_notes.c06_additional_cybersecurity_testing: untrusted-dimension inputs: fuzz image width/height/stride combos in the native harness.

npm/helmet.assessment: Security-hardening middleware maintained by an author deeply versed in web security; the package's entire purpose is SBD for the HTTP layer.

criterion_notes.c11_security_by_design_indicators: the component exists to implement secure defaults; documentation of header semantics is exemplary.

npm/fabric.assessment: Fabric.js org-maintained canvas engine rendering user-influenced drawing templates in the web editor; parsing SVG/JSON project content puts it on an untrusted-input path.

criterion_notes.c06_additional_cybersecurity_testing: SVG/JSON import paths are untrusted: include in web fuzzing and XSS review.
